name: Backburner
subtitle: Your iPhone helps your Mac run a 27B model
description: The Backburner iPhone app: plug the phone into your Mac with a 10 Gb/s USB-C cable and it runs part of Qwen3.8-27B (faster prompt reading) and holds context the Mac has no room for. You also need the Mac side: https://github.com/StayLameBro/backburner

apps.name: Backburner
apps.subtitle: Your iPhone as a second GPU for your Mac
apps.localizedDescription:
Plug the phone into your Mac with a 10 Gb/s USB-C cable, open Backburner and keep it in front. The Mac's server (scripts/serve.sh) then sends the phone layers 41-64 of each prompt batch and, past 64k tokens, the oldest part of the context.

Needs an iPhone 15 Pro or newer (the 17 Pro gets the most from it) or an M-series iPad (untested so far) and the Mac side from github.com/StayLameBro/backburner. Very early: please post your results in the repo.

versions.localizedDescription: Security fix, please update. Over the USB cable the app now answers only the Mac on the other end, and it no longer announces itself on the network. Wi-Fi stays off unless you pair the phone over the cable (scripts/phone-wifi.sh); then it is encrypted and needs that key.
Installs on iPads too (M-series; untested, please post results). The app's text says iPad on an iPad, and it runs full screen there.

privacy.NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription: Backburner lets the Mac find this phone on the USB cable.
